details:
Foremost i know reading all the stuff on the icanny can probably be draining by the VRChat dev team, so I wanted to say in this post to congratulate the team for not pulling all their hair out reading the icanny and for making an amazing contribution to the growth and success of the platform. I honestly want to congratulate everyone for doing an outstanding an amazing job on this game/VR experience. I've been on this game for a very long time (early 2017) and I believe the devs should be recognized for the amazing work that they have done and the challenges they have overcame. Honestly great work! I think the VRChat team has tackled some of the most complex problems moving VR forward in technology and I think this platform will be an example for VR experienced to follow. 
I have a lot of love for VRChat and it's culture that perhaps I would hate to ever have it die-out or become influenced by extreme dramatic changes; like changes in business structure and user experience catering towards a more mainstream or professional audience. I often think that this game could become a dramatically different experience in the future if influenced by a different vision. If monetization and industry influence is to influence the game's culture, I think it would change this unique VRChat culture into something drastically different than what it is today; therefore, I propose an idea. If VRChat were to change to a more corporate structure with a focus on monetization, publicity, industry status and value, investor funding, a wider audience demographic that expands into untapped markets (perhaps such as purchasing avatar clothing, more paid internal AAA quality games/experiences, perhaps internal monetary human services (like paid VR therapy, rehab, yoga, fitness, comedy, and workshops),  and other robust monetary features) and develop a more mainsteam-market-comparable industry vision, I believe it would be a good idea to release a "VRChat 2.0" or another version of VRChat and leave the first version of VRChat the same without the influence of industry and business. I think having two separate versions can be a large leap forward and maintain an audiences catering towards the desired experience they want to play or participate in. If a VRChat 2.0 is made, perhaps this version of VRChat can be a clean, professional, mainstreamed centralized, optimized and improved upon where the old version also remains to exists which can be seen as maybe more of a wild version with more liberties with creative freedom, and to create a different kind of user experience for a less mainstream audience. Overall, I hope the VRChat culture stays strong and lives long. That wraps up my biggest suggestion. Thank you for making such a great game and VR experience.
title: Community love and a quick suggestion for the future of VRChat.
